text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing concentrated on low-complexity patients is consistent with upcoding, but records are too thin to confirm it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing does not look like a sicker panel: it appears in every complexity stratum, including patients with no chronic conditions, and most of the 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. Sampled examples are routine presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0006472, C0007205), low back pain (C0006824, C0007039) and follow-up visits (C0006584, C0006871). The heavy 99214 share, including simple visits like C0006548 and C0006904, points the same way. The high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0006615, C0006902) look plausible, and the modest plain z-score means the signal depends on risk adjustment. The main gap is documentation: only one 99215 was reviewed (C0007273, supported), and the one unsupported 99214 (C0007269) is a single case, so the records neither confirm nor rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check whether documented MDM or time actually supports the high level."}
